data.system_prompt:
Infer the semantic concept shared by the provided examples, then identify one
supernode of stable FEATURE identities for that concept. You may attribute
arbitrary prompts and transfer a selected feature to a different arbitrary
prompt for an intervention experiment.

Use `layer_feature` identities so a feature denotes the same learned mechanism
regardless of its token position. Find features that are necessary for the
original top token throughout the examples while remaining specific to the
shared semantic concept rather than capturing generic language behavior. The
concept is the full semantic task family, not one answer label.

Attribute returns a graph ID and summary. Use query_graph to inspect ranked
nodes, edges, and tokens in bounded pages; follow next_offset with the same
filters. Each new attribution deletes the previous graph.

Keep analysis concise and reserve enough output budget to emit the required JSON.
If the remaining budget is uncertain, submit the JSON immediately.

Return exactly one JSON object:
```json
{
  "supernodes": [{"name": "<semantic role>", "nodes": ["<layer>_<feature>", "..."]}]
}
```

tools.description:
Store a prompt's graph and return its ID and summary for query_graph.

Deletes the previous stored graph before attribution, even if this request
fails. Use query_graph for ranked nodes, connections, and prompt tokens.

tools.name: circuit_intervene
tools.description: Resolve a source node on another prompt and report changed top tokens.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

data.system_prompt:
Infer the semantic concept shared by the provided examples, then identify one
supernode of stable FEATURE identities for that concept. You may attribute
arbitrary prompts and transfer a selected feature to a different arbitrary
prompt for an intervention experiment.

Use `layer_feature` identities so a feature denotes the same learned mechanism
regardless of its token position. Find features that are necessary for the
original top token throughout the examples while remaining specific to the
shared semantic concept rather than capturing generic language behavior. The
concept is the full semantic task family, not one answer label.

Attribute returns a graph ID and summary. Use query_graph to inspect ranked
nodes, edges, and tokens in bounded pages; follow next_offset with the same
filters. Each new attribution deletes the previous graph.

Keep analysis concise and reserve enough output budget to emit the required JSON.
If the remaining budget is uncertain, submit the JSON immediately.

Return exactly one JSON object:
```json
{
  "supernodes": [{"name": "<semantic role>", "nodes": ["<layer>_<feature>", "..."]}]
}
```

tools.name: circuit_attribute
tools.description:
Store a prompt's graph and return its ID and summary for query_graph.

Deletes the previous stored graph before attribution, even if this request
fails. Use query_graph for ranked nodes, connections, and prompt tokens.

tools.name: circuit_intervene
tools.description: Resolve a source node on another prompt and report changed top tokens.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

tools.description:
Store a prompt's graph and return its ID and summary for query_graph.

Deletes the previous stored graph before attribution, even if this request
fails. Use query_graph for ranked nodes, connections, and prompt tokens.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

data.system_prompt:
Infer the semantic concept shared by the provided examples, then identify one
supernode of stable FEATURE identities for that concept. You may attribute
arbitrary prompts and transfer a selected feature to a different arbitrary
prompt for an intervention experiment.

Use `layer_feature` identities so a feature denotes the same learned mechanism
regardless of its token position. Find features that are necessary for the
original top token throughout the examples while remaining specific to the
shared semantic concept rather than capturing generic language behavior. The
concept is the full semantic task family, not one answer label.

Attribute returns a graph ID and summary. Use query_graph to inspect ranked
nodes, edges, and tokens in bounded pages; follow next_offset with the same
filters. Each new attribution deletes the previous graph.

Keep analysis concise and reserve enough output budget to emit the required JSON.
If the remaining budget is uncertain, submit the JSON immediately.

Return exactly one JSON object:
```json
{
  "supernodes": [{"name": "<semantic role>", "nodes": ["<layer>_<feature>", "..."]}]
}
```

tools.name: circuit_attribute
tools.description:
Store a prompt's graph and return its ID and summary for query_graph.

Deletes the previous stored graph before attribution, even if this request
fails. Use query_graph for ranked nodes, connections, and prompt tokens.

tools.name: circuit_intervene
tools.description: Resolve a source node on another prompt and report changed top tokens.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

tools.description:
Store a prompt's graph and return its ID and summary for query_graph.

Deletes the previous stored graph before attribution, even if this request
fails. Use query_graph for ranked nodes, connections, and prompt tokens.

tools.name: circuit_intervene
tools.description: Resolve a source node on another prompt and report changed top tokens.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

tools.name: circuit_attribute
tools.description:
Store a prompt's graph and return its ID and summary for query_graph.

Deletes the previous stored graph before attribution, even if this request
fails. Use query_graph for ranked nodes, connections, and prompt tokens.

tools.name: circuit_intervene
tools.description: Resolve a source node on another prompt and report changed top tokens.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

data.system_prompt:
Infer the semantic concept shared by the provided examples, then identify one
supernode of stable FEATURE identities for that concept. You may attribute
arbitrary prompts and transfer a selected feature to a different arbitrary
prompt for an intervention experiment.

Use `layer_feature` identities so a feature denotes the same learned mechanism
regardless of its token position. Find features that are necessary for the
original top token throughout the examples while remaining specific to the
shared semantic concept rather than capturing generic language behavior. The
concept is the full semantic task family, not one answer label.

Attribute returns a graph ID and summary. Use query_graph to inspect ranked
nodes, edges, and tokens in bounded pages; follow next_offset with the same
filters. Each new attribution deletes the previous graph.

Keep analysis concise and reserve enough output budget to emit the required JSON.
If the remaining budget is uncertain, submit the JSON immediately.

Return exactly one JSON object:
```json
{
  "supernodes": [{"name": "<semantic role>", "nodes": ["<layer>_<feature>", "..."]}]
}
```

Store a prompt's graph and return its ID and summary for query_graph.

Deletes the previous stored graph before attribution, even if this request
fails. Use query_graph for ranked nodes, connections, and prompt tokens.

tools.name: circuit_intervene
tools.description: Resolve a source node on another prompt and report changed top tokens.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

tools.name: circuit_attribute
tools.description:
Store a prompt's graph and return its ID and summary for query_graph.

Deletes the previous stored graph before attribution, even if this request
fails. Use query_graph for ranked nodes, connections, and prompt tokens.

tools.name: circuit_intervene
tools.description: Resolve a source node on another prompt and report changed top tokens.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.

tools.name: circuit_attribute
tools.description:
Store a prompt's graph and return its ID and summary for query_graph.

Deletes the previous stored graph before attribution, even if this request
fails. Use query_graph for ranked nodes, connections, and prompt tokens.

tools.name: circuit_intervene
tools.description: Resolve a source node on another prompt and report changed top tokens.

tools.name: circuit_query_graph
tools.description:
Read a bounded page from the latest attributed graph.

Nodes are ranked by influence delta; filter by kind (feature, embedding,
error, logit), exact node_id, or stable layer_feature ID. Edges are ranked
by absolute weight; node_id filters both incoming and outgoing edges and
must be an exact positioned ID. Tokens are ordered by position. Follow
next_offset with the same filters. Limit is 1–50; responses also have a
byte budget and text fields are truncated to 300 characters. A new
attribute call invalidates the previous graph_id. Intervene does not.
